chosen.premise: Haunter’s tongue is made of gas, and one lick causes shaking that lasts until death.
chosen.hook: Haunter’s tongue isn’t flesh—it’s gas, and its lick never lets you stop shaking.
chosen.visualIdea: Zoom into a gaseous tongue, then show a victim’s shaking meter rising without stopping.
chosen.note: A gaseous tongue causing unstoppable shaking until death is exceptionally specific, disturbing, well-supported across multiple entries, and highly visual.

candidates.premise: Haunter is 1.6 meters tall but weighs only 0.1 kilograms.
candidates.hook: This 1.6-meter Pokémon weighs less than a full glass of water.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Haunter beside a 1.6-meter ruler, then smash-cut to a scale reading 0.1 kg.
candidates.note: The extreme height-to-weight contrast is concrete and easy to visualize, though weight comparisons can work for many floating Pokémon.

candidates.premise: Haunter can slip through any obstacle, then lurk inside walls to watch its foes.
candidates.hook: The wall between you and Haunter does absolutely nothing.
candidates.visualIdea: A room assembles around a person as Haunter’s eyes appear inside the walls.
candidates.note: The combination of phasing through obstacles and hiding inside walls to watch foes is distinctly Haunter and gives strong horror visuals.

candidates.premise: Haunter fears light so much that bright cities may be pushing it toward extinction.
candidates.hook: Streetlights might be driving Haunter extinct.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen a moonless, dark street with Haunter versus a brightly lit city where it fades away.
candidates.note: The possible extinction angle is surprising and supported, but the premise depends on a single entry and “driving extinct” slightly overstates “may be on the verge.”

candidates.premise: Haunter’s most dangerous trap is a beckoning gesture from darkness: approaching it lets it steal your life.
candidates.hook: If Haunter beckons from the dark, running toward it is the worst choice.
candidates.visualIdea: A silhouetted Haunter beckons from darkness while warning text flashes: “Do not approach.”
candidates.note: The warning not to approach a beckoning Haunter is well-supported and cinematic, but the stalking-from-darkness idea overlaps with generic ghost-horror framing.

candidates.premise: Haunter evolves from Gastly at level 25, but reaching Gengar requires a trade instead.
candidates.hook: Haunter’s evolution path changes the rules halfway through.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Gastly leveling to 25 into Haunter, then freeze until a trade link transforms it into Gengar.
candidates.note: The switch from level-based evolution to trading is a clear, useful contradiction, but the evolution-method evidence is trusted secondary rather than official.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; this choice already has the best combination of Haunter-specificity, surprise, concrete premise, visual potential, and direct multi-entry support.
